one_sentence_idea: Condition segmentation networks directly on physical voxel spacing via FiLM-style metadata injection instead of resampling every volume to a canonical grid.
main_risk: Spacing effects may be absorbable by heavy resampling augmentation, making conditioning redundant.

one_sentence_idea: Replace mask prediction for vessels/airways with prediction of a centerline flow field (direction + radius) from which the mask is reconstructed, to make connectivity the primary learned quantity.
main_risk: Reconstruction from noisy fields may introduce its own failure modes (hallucinated bridges).

one_sentence_idea: Train segmentation models to predict the full inter-rater mask distribution and evaluate them against a fresh, unseen rater rather than a majority-vote consensus.
main_risk: Few public datasets have enough raters for statistically meaningful held-out-rater evaluation.

one_sentence_idea: Optimize segmentation networks directly for downstream biomarker error (volume, diameter, ejection fraction) with the biomarker computed differentiably from the soft mask.
main_risk: Biomarker terms may trade bias for variance, worsening per-case reliability.

one_sentence_idea: Derive physically correct soft boundary labels from partial-volume modeling (fraction of tissue per voxel) instead of hard binary labels at object borders.
main_risk: Contour GT itself may be too imprecise for the PSF model to add signal.

one_sentence_idea: Quantify and eliminate sliding-window seam inconsistency by adding a shifted-crop prediction-consistency loss during training.
main_risk: The variance may be small for organs and only matter for tiny lesions, narrowing the contribution.

one_sentence_idea: Replace naive left-right flip augmentation with laterality-aware flipping that swaps paired labels, and audit how much silent damage naive flipping causes.
main_risk: Modern high-capacity models may already resolve laterality from context, nullifying the effect at scale.

one_sentence_idea: Feed acquisition metadata (reconstruction kernel, kVp, MRI sequence parameters) into the segmentation network as conditioning tokens instead of discarding DICOM headers.
main_risk: Metadata may be too coarse a proxy for actual appearance variation, or headers unreliable in the wild.

one_sentence_idea: Use an implicit (coordinate-based) decoder queried at physical world coordinates so one model trains on and predicts at arbitrary anisotropic resolutions without resampling.
main_risk: INR decoders may underfit fine in-plane detail, trading one failure for another.

one_sentence_idea: Train a segmentation quality-control head that predicts per-case Dice/surface error without ground truth, supervised on the model's own historical errors, to gate deployment.
main_risk: QC heads may inherit the same blind spots as the segmenter (correlated failures).

one_sentence_idea: Build a physics-based metal artifact simulator (beam hardening, photon starvation on inserted implant shapes) as targeted augmentation for CT segmentation around implants.
main_risk: Simulator-real gap in artifact texture may cap transfer.

one_sentence_idea: Train one backbone across datasets with contradictory labeling protocols by attaching per-dataset "protocol heads" that model each dataset's definition (e.g., liver ± vessels) explicitly.
main_risk: Insufficient per-protocol data to fit heads; protocol differences may be too subtle to matter.

one_sentence_idea: Segment longitudinal change directly from image pairs (change mask as output) instead of segmenting each timepoint and subtracting after registration.
main_risk: Synthetic change used for training may not cover real growth patterns.

one_sentence_idea: Exploit unlabeled test-retest repeat scans as a free training signal by penalizing prediction disagreement between same-patient repeats.
main_risk: Consistency may be achieved by degenerate over-smoothing (must monitor accuracy).

one_sentence_idea: Learn an end-to-end differentiable zoom policy that selects where to run high-resolution segmentation for tiny structures (optic chiasm, cranial nerves) instead of fixed two-stage cropping.
main_risk: Memory cost of joint training; variants may be too rare in training data for the policy to learn them.

one_sentence_idea: Output an explicit third "uncertain band" class calibrated to inter-rater variability so downstream users review only the band, not the whole mask.
main_risk: Coverage calibration may not survive domain shift, which is where it is most needed.

one_sentence_idea: Replace fixed 0.5 thresholding of soft masks with a decision-theoretic per-case threshold chosen to maximize expected Dice/minimize expected volume error under the model's own predictive distribution.
main_risk: Requires reasonably calibrated probabilities; badly calibrated models may not benefit without recalibration.

one_sentence_idea: For airway/vessel trees, deliberately oversegment with a high-recall network, then prune with a learned graph classifier operating on branch-level features.
main_risk: Proposal stage may miss branches unrecoverably, capping the ceiling.

one_sentence_idea: Test whether topological loss benefits survive being computed on 4×–8× downsampled probability maps, making persistent-homology training affordable for 3D.
main_risk: Fine-scale topology errors (thin bridges) may be exactly the ones that matter and the ones lost at coarse scale.

one_sentence_idea: Constrain organ segmentation outputs to a learned discrete codebook of plausible shapes (VQ shape prior) so the network cannot emit anatomically impossible masks.
main_risk: Codebook may fail on genuine pathology-induced shape outliers — precisely the important cases.

one_sentence_idea: Segment directly from undersampled k-space (jointly with implicit reconstruction) instead of segmenting DL-reconstructed images, to avoid committing to reconstruction errors.
main_risk: Requires raw k-space with segmentation labels — limited public overlap.

one_sentence_idea: Give MRI segmentation networks per-scan self-calibration tokens that predict intensity landmarks (CSF/GM/WM modes) and normalize features internally, replacing offline histogram standardization.
main_risk: Landmark prediction itself may fail under the same shifts it is meant to fix (circularity).

one_sentence_idea: Replace foreground-oversampled patch training with dual-stream training (whole-volume low-res context + local high-res patch) to fix false positives far from the target organ.
main_risk: Whole-body data may be needed at training time, which some datasets lack.

one_sentence_idea: Train multiple-lesion segmentation with a lesion-instance detection objective (per-lesion F1) alongside voxel loss, because semantic Dice hides missed small lesions.
main_risk: Instance surrogates may be unstable for touching/confluent lesions.

one_sentence_idea: Enforce cyclic temporal consistency across the cardiac cycle in cine MRI segmentation using unlabeled frames, with labeled end-diastole/end-systole only.
main_risk: Arrhythmic patients violate cyclicity — must detect and exempt them.

one_sentence_idea: Jointly predict per-slice motion-corruption scores and use them to reweight inter-slice feature fusion for fetal/neonatal MRI segmentation.
main_risk: Real motion artifacts differ from simulated ones in structured ways.

one_sentence_idea: Formulate 3D interactive correction as a conditional update network: one corrected slice (or scribble) plus current prediction in, corrected volume out — optimizing clicks-to-acceptable, not Dice.
main_risk: Simulated click behavior may not match real annotators (needs small user study eventually).

one_sentence_idea: Characterize and correct structure-size-dependent miscalibration: fit size-conditional temperature/threshold corrections so small structures stop being systematically mis-confident.
main_risk: Effect may be dataset-idiosyncratic rather than a general law.

one_sentence_idea: Make multi-sequence MRI tumor models robust to missing sequences by conditioning on an explicit presence mask and training with structured sequence dropout, instead of zero-filling absent channels.
main_risk: Combinatorial evaluation cost; conclusions may vary by tumor sub-region.

one_sentence_idea: Detect and exploit "anatomical addressability": predict each voxel's coordinates in a canonical body atlas as an auxiliary task, giving the network an explicit positional prior for organ layout.
main_risk: Coarse registration noise may cap the value of the auxiliary signal.

one_sentence_idea: Replace uniform random masking in medical masked-image-modeling with anatomy-weighted masking that allocates mask budget by local anatomical information density.
main_risk: Weighted masking may just replicate what longer uniform training achieves (a constant-factor, not qualitative, gain).

one_sentence_idea: Run a controlled scaling-law study for 3D medical foundation models that separates the axes of dataset size, voxel resolution, and patient diversity.
main_risk: Small-scale exponents may not extrapolate; conclusions could be architecture-specific.

one_sentence_idea: Tokenize medical volumes with content-adaptive supervoxels instead of fixed cubic patches, so token boundaries align with anatomical boundaries.
main_risk: Irregular tokens complicate positional encoding and efficient batching; engineering overhead may eat the gains.

one_sentence_idea: Build CT foundation models that treat Hounsfield units as calibrated physical measurements — enforcing quantitative-intensity equivariance instead of normalizing intensities away.
main_risk: HU calibration is imperfect in practice (kernel/kVp dependence), weakening the invariance.

one_sentence_idea: Systematically audit train-test contamination between medical FM pretraining corpora and popular benchmarks via near-duplicate patient/scan detection, and publish decontaminated benchmark splits.
main_risk: Duplicate detection thresholds are contestable; overlap may turn out negligible (a null result, though still publishable hygiene).

one_sentence_idea: Retrieval-augmented segmentation: retrieve the most similar labeled cases from a reference library at inference and condition the decoder on their image-mask pairs.
main_risk: Retrieval may leak benchmark near-duplicates, faking gains (ties to B-0035 audit).

one_sentence_idea: Train a medical in-context segmentation model (prompt with k example image-mask pairs, segment the query) and measure how in-context ability scales with pretraining task diversity, not data volume.
main_risk: Compute-hungry; conclusions may be capacity-dependent.

one_sentence_idea: Map where parameter-efficient adaptation must be placed in volumetric transformers: test the hypothesis that appearance shift requires early-layer adapters while label/task shift requires late-layer adapters.
main_risk: Findings may not generalize across FM architectures.

one_sentence_idea: Prevent catastrophic forgetting when fine-tuning medical FMs on narrow tasks by rehearsing on self-generated pseudo-labeled diverse anatomy instead of stored data.
main_risk: Pseudo-label errors may reinforce and amplify existing FM biases.

one_sentence_idea: Measure whether medical FMs memorize rare patients — via membership-inference and near-copy reconstruction attacks on MIM-pretrained models — and identify which pretraining choices modulate it.
main_risk: Small-model results may understate or overstate large-model memorization.

one_sentence_idea: Federated pretraining of a multi-modality medical FM using locally routed modality experts over a shared anatomical trunk, so sites never share raw data or modality-specific experts.
main_risk: Simulated federation understates real-world heterogeneity (compute, dropout, protocol drift).

one_sentence_idea: Characterize the frequency-response bias of medical FMs (which spatial-frequency bands their features preserve) and correct it with band-balanced pretraining perturbations.
main_risk: Frequency deficits may be dataset artifacts (reconstruction kernels) rather than model properties.

one_sentence_idea: Entropy-adaptive token merging for whole-body volumes: aggressively merge tokens in homogeneous regions while preserving full resolution in complex regions, to make whole-body transformers tractable.
main_risk: Complexity estimator itself may miss subtle lesions (chicken-and-egg).

one_sentence_idea: Define an "acquisition-sensitivity fingerprint" benchmark: measure every medical FM's output sensitivity to controlled acquisition-parameter perturbations (kernel, dose, sequence, spacing) as a standard model card entry.
main_risk: Simulated perturbations may not span real protocol variation.

one_sentence_idea: Localize where demographic performance bias enters medical FMs by swapping pretraining and fine-tuning populations factorially and measuring per-group segmentation quality.
main_risk: Confounding between demographics and scanners/sites in available data.

one_sentence_idea: Open-vocabulary medical segmentation where class queries are embeddings of ontology graph nodes (RadLex/SNOMED), enabling zero-shot segmentation of unseen structures via graph proximity.
main_risk: Ontology distance may correlate poorly with visual similarity for some organ families.

one_sentence_idea: Continual (streaming) pretraining of medical FMs across sequentially arriving sites, using generative replay of synthetic exemplars instead of stored patient data.
main_risk: Generative replay quality for 3D may be insufficient to preserve protocol-specific features.

one_sentence_idea: Distill 3D FMs into 2.5D slice-wise students with cross-slice consistency distillation, simultaneously quantifying how much genuinely 3D information the teacher actually uses.
main_risk: Distillation losses may confound the measurement (student capacity limits mistaken for 3D value).

one_sentence_idea: Probe whether medical FM embedding geometry preserves anatomical topology (adjacency, containment) and use the topology-preservation score to predict transfer performance.
main_risk: Correlation may exist but be driven by a confounder (model scale).

one_sentence_idea: Establish a frozen-feature dense-probing benchmark for medical FMs and test whether FM rankings flip between linear probing and full fine-tuning.
main_risk: Probe design choices (decoder capacity) could themselves determine rankings.

one_sentence_idea: Pretrain medical FMs by solving dense multi-scale registration between unlabeled scan pairs, on the hypothesis that correspondence is a better dense pretext than reconstruction.
main_risk: Registration pretext may collapse on non-alignable pairs (different body regions) without careful pair mining.

one_sentence_idea: Characterize test-time compute scaling for segmentation FMs: does quality scale with inference-time sampling (multiple stochastic decodes + agreement-based selection/merging), and where does it saturate?
main_risk: Existing models may lack enough output diversity for selection to help (would require diversity-trained decoders).

one_sentence_idea: Pretrain a modality-agnostic FM with aggressive cross-modality dropout (CT/MR/US of overlapping anatomy) to force a shared anatomical latent, then test zero-shot cross-modality segmentation transfer.
main_risk: Without paired data, the latent may align coarse anatomy only, failing at boundary precision.

one_sentence_idea: Measure resolution/patch-size transfer curves for medical FMs and fix scale brittleness with scale-randomized pretraining.
main_risk: Scale randomization may dilute pretraining signal, trading peak for robustness.

one_sentence_idea: Replace learned positional embeddings with body-coordinate embeddings derived from scout/localizer registration, so FM tokens know where in the body they are.
main_risk: Coordinate estimation fails exactly on unusual scans where it is most needed.

one_sentence_idea: Use the FM's own pretraining signal (e.g., masked-reconstruction error maps) as a free, training-free spatial error predictor for downstream segmentation QC.
main_risk: Reconstruction difficulty may track texture complexity, not semantic error.

one_sentence_idea: Test whether aggressive dedup + diversity-pruning of medical pretraining corpora (removing near-identical slices/series) lets a 10× smaller corpus match full-corpus FM quality.
main_risk: Rare-case removal by overzealous pruning could hurt exactly the tail robustness that matters.

one_sentence_idea: Train mixture-of-experts medical FMs and test whether unsupervised expert routing spontaneously discovers pathology (routing as a free abnormality detector).
main_risk: Experts may specialize on acquisition parameters (scanner) rather than pathology.

one_sentence_idea: Add a cross-scale feature-consistency objective to medical FM pretraining so that structures produce stable features across the resolution pyramid, targeting lesions visible only at particular scales.
main_risk: Consistency may over-smooth scale-specific information that is genuinely scale-local.

one_sentence_idea: Cross-patient anatomical contrastive pretraining: use registration-derived correspondence to make "same anatomical location, different patient" the positive pair, instead of augmentation-based positives.
main_risk: Registration errors inject label noise into positives; pathology violates cross-patient correspondence.

one_sentence_idea: Reformulate smoke segmentation as alpha-matte/optical-density regression instead of binary masking, because smoke physically has no boundary.
main_risk: Composited training data may not span real in-the-wild smoke/illumination interactions.

one_sentence_idea: Create physically grounded smoke ground truth by capturing smoke in front of calibrated patterned backgrounds, recovering true per-pixel transmittance analytically.
main_risk: Lab smoke (glycol fog) may differ optically from combustion smoke; needs at least one real-smoke validation session.

one_sentence_idea: Use turbulence statistics of motion (temporal power spectra of local flow) as a self-supervised signature separating smoke from fog, clouds, and dust.
main_risk: Requires sufficient frame rate and resolution; distant plumes may be too small for reliable spectral estimation.

one_sentence_idea: Exploit flame flicker frequency structure (via high-fps or event cameras) as a near-invariant fire signature to kill sunset/brake-light/reflection false positives.
main_risk: Wind-driven distant flames and near-smoldering fires may lack detectable flicker.

one_sentence_idea: Use polarization imaging as the primary cue for transparent-object segmentation, with a controlled study of when polarization is necessary versus when RGB context suffices.
main_risk: Polarization cues degrade outdoors/under diffuse lighting; conclusions may be lighting-regime-specific.

one_sentence_idea: Mine LiDAR/ToF dropout and range-anomaly regions from robot logs as free weak labels for training RGB-only transparent-surface segmentation.
main_risk: Dropout also occurs on dark/absorptive and distant surfaces — confounders that filtering may not fully remove.

one_sentence_idea: Segment transparent objects by predicting the background-distortion (refraction) field and deriving the object mask from where distortion is non-zero.
main_risk: Estimating the undistorted background in cluttered real scenes may be too ill-posed without multi-view input.

one_sentence_idea: Replace masks with two-layer scene decomposition (foreground alpha + occluded background estimate) as the standard output for semi-transparent categories, with an evaluation protocol built on composited ground truth.
main_risk: Two-layer assumption breaks for multiple stacked transparent media.

one_sentence_idea: Develop and validate soft-boundary evaluation metrics for fuzzy objects by measuring which candidate metrics best predict human quality judgments of smoke/fire masks.
main_risk: Human judgments may be task-dependent (alarm vs. quantification), requiring multiple protocols.

one_sentence_idea: Collect multi-annotator labels on smoke/transparent boundaries and train ambiguity-calibrated models that predict the annotator distribution, testing whether model uncertainty can match human disagreement geography.
main_risk: Annotation cost; disagreement may partly reflect tool/interface artifacts.

one_sentence_idea: Run a controlled physics-fidelity ablation for synthetic smoke training data: which simulation components (scattering order, illumination model, turbulence resolution) actually matter for sim-to-real transfer.
main_risk: Interactions between axes may defeat the factorial budget; conclusions may depend on the real-domain lighting.

one_sentence_idea: Separate steam/water vapor from smoke using condensation dynamics — the characteristic dissipation, buoyancy, and boundary-evolution differences over seconds-scale windows.
main_risk: Distance/resolution limits temporal cues; mixed steam+smoke scenes remain hard.

one_sentence_idea: For static cameras, learn a background radiance model and detect smoke as the residual consistent with a scattering forward model — self-supervised, no smoke masks needed.
main_risk: Illumination changes and moving objects violate the background model; airlight A estimation is fragile at night.

one_sentence_idea: Repurpose pretrained dehazing networks' transmission-map estimators as zero-shot smoke segmenters, testing whether dehazing is secretly the strongest smoke prior available.
main_risk: Dehazing models assume global atmospheric haze and may fail structurally on localized plumes.

one_sentence_idea: Supervise smoke density estimation using visibility of fiducial landmarks at known distances (industrial sites, fire ranges), converting landmark contrast loss into calibrated optical-depth labels.
main_risk: Sparse sightlines may under-constrain dense interpolation; illumination variation contaminates contrast measurements.

one_sentence_idea: Inject buoyant-plume physics (rise, bend-over under wind, entrainment growth rates) as a structured shape prior for aerial/tower wildfire smoke segmentation.
main_risk: Terrain-driven plume distortion and multiple merged plumes break the parametric families.

one_sentence_idea: Distill thermal-camera supervision (which sees through smoke and sees fire directly) into RGB-only fire/smoke models via co-mounted capture rigs.
main_risk: Registration errors between modalities; thermal supervision may teach cues absent in RGB (unlearnable targets).

one_sentence_idea: Build a hard-negative stress benchmark for fire segmentation (sunsets, sodium lights, reflections, red foliage, welding) and show that radiometric cues from HDR/raw capture separate what tone-mapped RGB cannot.
main_risk: Licensing/collection effort for diverse confusers; raw capture subset is small.

one_sentence_idea: Train fire/smoke perception directly on raw sensor data (pre-ISP), hypothesizing that ISP processing (white balance, tone mapping, denoising) destroys the radiometric signatures of combustion.
main_risk: Raw data availability at scale; cross-sensor raw generalization is poor.

one_sentence_idea: Detect glass surfaces from the parallax behavior of specular highlights under small camera motion — highlights move against the background flow — as a self-supervised video cue.
main_risk: Textureless backgrounds give no flow to be anomalous against; motion blur corrupts the cue.

one_sentence_idea: Segment glass scenes into transmitted vs. reflected content (what is behind the glass vs. mirrored) as a three-way dense decomposition, since downstream tasks need the distinction, not just "glass here."
main_risk: Real glass has spatially varying reflectance and dirt; two-layer compositing may undershoot complexity.

one_sentence_idea: Recover 3D smoke occupancy from sparse multi-view cameras (differentiable volumetric rendering with a scattering model), making segmentation a 2D projection of an estimated 3D medium.
main_risk: Calibration drift and highly dynamic media may break slow volumetric optimization; needs a fast amortized variant.

one_sentence_idea: Transfer fuzzy-media segmentation machinery (opacity regression, soft-boundary metrics) to ground-glass opacities in lung CT, treating GGO as "smoke inside the body."
main_risk: Attenuation baselines vary with inspiration level and scanner, confounding density labels.

one_sentence_idea: Model ultrasound acoustic shadows as first-class ambiguous regions: jointly predict shadow maps (from attenuation physics) and shadow-aware anatomy segmentation with explicit "no-evidence" outputs.
main_risk: Distinguishing shadow from genuinely hypoechoic tissue is itself uncertain.

one_sentence_idea: Harvest free supervision from surveillance timelapses that capture the same static scene with and without smoke, using the clean frame as the known background in a compositing model.
main_risk: Illumination differences between before/during frames corrupt the derivation; needs illumination normalization.

one_sentence_idea: Build a diagnostic taxonomy-benchmark that decomposes "hard segmentation" by boundary-evidence type (transparent, translucent-media, camouflage, shadow, motion-blur) and tests whether methods fail differently per type.
main_risk: Type purity is hard to guarantee; datasets confound type with domain (indoor/outdoor).

one_sentence_idea: Output nested core/extent masks for fuzzy objects — a certain inner core and a maximal outer extent — and annotate datasets this way, which is cheaper and better-posed than single-contour annotation.
main_risk: Two boundaries could be slower in practice; tooling must support it.

one_sentence_idea: Solve occlusion ordering through transparency — instance segmentation of stacked/nested glassware with correct depth ordering — using ray-traced synthetic training and real lab-glassware evaluation.
main_risk: Real-world dirt, liquids, and labels on glass may dominate the difficulty rather than the formulation.

one_sentence_idea: Disentangle intrinsic smoke density from illumination/background context by training on multi-illumination captures of identical plumes, forcing appearance-invariant density estimates.
main_risk: Capturing identical plumes under multiple illuminations is physically tricky (plumes evolve); needs fast lighting switching.

one_sentence_idea: Formulate early smoke detection as sequential evidence accumulation with an explicit detection-latency-vs-false-alarm operating curve, instead of per-frame segmentation.
main_risk: Camera vibration and compression artifacts may dominate the weak temporal signal at long range.

one_sentence_idea: Solve the test-time-adaptation model-selection problem with a label-free surrogate validation signal (cross-augmentation prediction agreement) validated against oracle selection.
main_risk: Surrogate may fail exactly under large shift, where selection matters most.

one_sentence_idea: Characterize the conditions under which entropy-minimization TTA collapses (class imbalance, small batches, long streams) and build a cheap online diagnostic that switches adaptation off before collapse.
main_risk: Early-warning signals may be method-specific, limiting generality.

one_sentence_idea: Disentangle covariate shift from label-distribution shift in BN-statistic adaptation: recalibrating BN on target batches silently conflates the two and mis-adapts when class prevalence differs.
main_risk: Class-conditional statistics estimated from wrong posteriors may self-reinforce errors.

one_sentence_idea: Measure the drift half-life of continual test-time adaptation on long realistic streams and fix accumulation with source-statistic anchoring plus stochastic parameter restoration.
main_risk: Realistic long streams with ground truth are scarce; may need semi-synthetic stream construction.

one_sentence_idea: Empirically decompose cross-site medical performance drop into scanner, protocol, and population components using matched-cohort counterfactual datasets.
main_risk: Public data may not contain enough matched structure; confounding may be irreducible.

one_sentence_idea: Establish a "shift-type → adaptation-locus" law: appearance shifts are correctable by normalization-layer adaptation alone, while geometric shifts require spatial-module adaptation, tested via controlled factorial shifts.
main_risk: Real shifts are mixtures; the routing rule must handle composition.

one_sentence_idea: Show that global Fourier-amplitude-swap adaptation fails on spatially localized domain differences (artifacts, coils, shading) and replace it with spatially windowed frequency alignment.
main_risk: Windowing introduces seam artifacts and more hyperparameters.

one_sentence_idea: Separate geometric domain shift (field-of-view, patient positioning, spacing) from appearance shift in DA benchmarks, and develop adaptation that re-estimates spatial priors rather than restyling intensities.
main_risk: Realistic geometric shift simulation must avoid trivial artifacts models could exploit.

one_sentence_idea: Mask pseudo-labels near predicted boundaries during self-training DA, since pseudo-label errors concentrate in boundary bands and drive error accumulation.
main_risk: For thin structures the band may swallow the whole object, requiring size-adaptive bands.

one_sentence_idea: Open-set domain adaptation for segmentation: detect and abstain on target-domain regions belonging to classes absent from the source label space, rather than force-labeling them.
main_risk: Novelty vs. shifted-known-class distinction may be fundamentally ambiguous at the pixel level.

one_sentence_idea: Active domain adaptation for segmentation that selects target regions (not images) to annotate, scored by the product of domain-discrepancy and decision-uncertainty.
main_risk: Region-level annotation cost models may not reflect real annotator time (context switching costs).

one_sentence_idea: Train a "shift meter" that predicts, per case, whether test-time adaptation will improve or harm the prediction — before running it — enabling selective adaptation.
main_risk: Delta-sign may depend on TTA method specifics, requiring per-method meters.

one_sentence_idea: Audit which self-supervised auxiliary losses actually correlate with segmentation improvement in single-image test-time training, across shift types — and expose anti-correlated ones.
main_risk: Findings may be architecture-specific; needs at least two backbones.

one_sentence_idea: Quantify lesion erasure/hallucination in GAN-based cross-domain image translation for segmentation DA, and prevent it with patch-level content-preservation contrastive constraints evaluated on lesion recall.
main_risk: The fixed detector used for measurement may itself be domain-sensitive (needs careful control).

one_sentence_idea: Replace learned style transfer with physics-derived acquisition mappings (e.g., CT kernel changes as measurable convolution kernels) for adaptation across reconstruction protocols.
main_risk: Many real shifts mix physical and non-physical components; scope must be honestly bounded.

one_sentence_idea: Adapt label-shift correction (prevalence reweighting via confusion-matrix EM) to dense segmentation outputs, correcting for sites whose pathology prevalence differs from the training distribution.
main_risk: Component-level independence assumptions may be too wrong for clustered pathology.

one_sentence_idea: Benchmark TTA under honest single-patient streaming (batch=1, no shuffling, no test-set reuse) and expose how much published gain depends on unrealistic batch composition.
main_risk: Faithful reimplementation burden; authors may dispute protocol choices (mitigate by releasing harness).

one_sentence_idea: Constrain test-time adaptation with an anatomical shape prior so that adaptation can change appearance processing but cannot push outputs off the manifold of plausible anatomy.
main_risk: The prior may block legitimate adaptation on genuinely unusual anatomy.

one_sentence_idea: Restrict test-time adaptation of dense transformers to a small set of learned tokens (adaptation-by-prompt), trading peak adaptation capacity for stability and revertibility.
main_risk: Token capacity may be insufficient for geometry-flavored shifts (consistent with B-0096's law).

one_sentence_idea: Domain versioning for streaming adaptation: detect when the input distribution reverts to a previously seen state (scanner switched back, protocol restored) and reload the cached adapted state instead of re-adapting.
main_risk: Fingerprint collisions between similar domains could load wrong states (needs confidence thresholds).

one_sentence_idea: Gradient-free feature adaptation via optimal-transport mapping of intermediate feature distributions at multiple depths, handling multimodal feature shifts that mean/variance alignment cannot express.
main_risk: OT estimation on small buffers is noisy; per-layer maps may compound errors.

one_sentence_idea: Build a taxonomy and detector for label-consistent shift — cases where appearance is in-distribution but the label convention differs — where any feature-level adaptation is guaranteed harmful.
main_risk: Real convention differences are subtler than simulated margin changes.

one_sentence_idea: Identify contrast inversion (structures flipping from bright to dark) as the dominant failure variable in cross-modality adaptation, and design sign-invariant edge representations that survive it.
main_risk: Inversion may be confounded with structure size/boundary strength.

one_sentence_idea: Adapt driving segmentation to adverse weather by first estimating physical weather parameters (fog density, rain rate) and conditioning the network on them, instead of treating weather as an unstructured domain.
main_risk: Real weather deviates from the scattering model (heterogeneous fog, spray), limiting the parametrization.

one_sentence_idea: Ship "source sketches" — a few hundred privacy-cleared synthetic exemplars distilled from the source model — alongside deployed models to close most of the source-free adaptation gap.
main_risk: Dense-prediction dataset distillation is technically immature; exemplars may leak more than audits detect.

one_sentence_idea: Adapt the input instead of the model: learn a per-case input-space transformation (frozen network, trainable preprocessing) so the deployed, certified model itself never changes.
main_risk: Appearance-only transforms cannot address geometry or semantic shift (consistent with B-0096).

one_sentence_idea: Order target-domain data easy-to-hard (by estimated shift magnitude) during self-training UDA, testing whether curriculum prevents early pseudo-label poisoning.
main_risk: Effect may be small relative to other pipeline noise; needs adequate seeds for power.

one_sentence_idea: Per-case source routing in multi-source adaptation: pick which source model (or mixture) to adapt from for each target case via fast embedding-space matching, instead of pooling all sources.
main_risk: Routing errors on truly novel targets could underperform the pooled model's safety-in-averaging.

one_sentence_idea: Session-level online adaptation of interactive segmentation models from the user's own corrections: every click is a free labeled pixel, so the model should get better within a reading session.
main_risk: Click simulators may overstate real-user consistency; adaptation could overfit to one user's style (feature or bug).

one_sentence_idea: A sealed, streaming, no-oracle benchmark harness for segmentation TTA that forbids target-label peeking, batch shuffling, and test-set reuse — with a public leaderboard re-running published methods.
main_risk: Faithful ports are laborious; authors may contest configurations (mitigated by accepting author-submitted configs).

one_sentence_idea: Audit and quantify "foreground bias" in few-shot segmentation — models segmenting the salient object regardless of what the support actually shows — via wrong-support counterfactual testing.
main_risk: Some benchmarks may legitimately lack distractor objects, making the audit less informative there.

one_sentence_idea: Suppress base-class leakage in novel-class segmentation by allocating novel classes an orthogonal feature subspace at episode time, rather than letting them compete inside base-class geometry.
main_risk: Orthogonalization may discard features the novel class genuinely needs.

one_sentence_idea: Construct a genuinely-novel-class benchmark (classes verifiably absent from web-scale pretraining) and measure how much "zero-shot segmentation" performance evaporates on it.
main_risk: Verifying absence from closed pretraining corpora is hard; fabricated objects may be unrepresentatively simple.

one_sentence_idea: Show that support-set selection explains more performance variance than method choice in FSS, and build active support selection (choosing which k examples to label) as the highest-leverage intervention.
main_risk: Coverage criteria that work on benchmarks may need class-specific tuning in the wild.

one_sentence_idea: Replace prototype averaging in k-shot segmentation with per-mode matching that preserves intra-class multimodality (a class with visually distinct sub-types keeps multiple prototypes).
main_risk: With small k, mode estimation is noisy; adaptive mode-count selection may be fragile.

one_sentence_idea: Fix support-query geometric mismatch (pose, viewpoint, scale) with lightweight test-time geometric alignment before feature correlation, instead of hoping correlation layers absorb it.
main_risk: Feature-space transforms may not correspond cleanly to image-space geometry for deep features.

one_sentence_idea: Add negative supports ("this is NOT the class") as a first-class input to few-shot segmentation, formalized as contrastive prototype construction.
main_risk: Untargeted negatives (random) may dilute rather than help — interface must guide negative choice.

one_sentence_idea: Disentangle recognition from delineation in FSS evaluation: measure separately whether the model found the right object and how well it drew the boundary, since these have different failure causes and cures.
main_risk: Decomposition requires instance-level GT which some FSS benchmarks lack (fixable on PASCAL/COCO-derived ones).

one_sentence_idea: Establish training-free FSS (frozen self-supervised features + correspondence + test-time optimization) as a mandatory baseline, quantifying exactly what episodic meta-training adds.
main_risk: Engineering effort in the baseline could be criticized as its own form of tuning (mitigate with ablations).

one_sentence_idea: Add novel classes to a deployed segmenter via null-space parameter updates that provably leave base-class outputs unchanged on a calibration set.
main_risk: Calibration-set null space may not cover the true base distribution; drift could appear off-calibration.

one_sentence_idea: Factor cross-domain FSS failure (natural-image supports/training → medical/industrial queries) into feature-transfer failure vs. matching-mechanism failure with swap experiments.
main_risk: In-domain components trained on small data may understate their ceiling, biasing attribution.

one_sentence_idea: Break the k-shot saturation of in-context segmentation (performance plateauing beyond ~5 shots) by replacing prompt concatenation with retrieval plus non-parametric decoding over all shots.
main_risk: Non-parametric decoding may be too slow for practical inference (though fine for the scientific question).

one_sentence_idea: Few-shot segmentation of relationally defined targets ("the handle of any tool", "the damaged part") where the class is a role, not an appearance category.
main_risk: Role definitions can be ambiguous; annotation consistency needs care.

one_sentence_idea: Characterize the extreme-minimal-supervision limit: one positive pixel (not a mask) per novel class, combined with strong class-agnostic segment priors.
main_risk: Results hinge on the quality of the class-agnostic prior, requiring multi-prior replication.

one_sentence_idea: Delineate the regimes where classical registration-based one-shot segmentation beats learned FSS in medical imaging (and vice versa), producing a decision rule instead of another method.
main_risk: Registration implementation quality strongly affects conclusions; must use strong, tuned baselines.

one_sentence_idea: Test whether diffusion-generated variations of support images (synthetic extra shots) improve FSS beyond classical augmentation, with generation conditioned to preserve the support mask.
main_risk: Mask-conditioned generation quality varies wildly across classes, confounding the analysis.

one_sentence_idea: Correct support-query appearance mismatch at test time by restyling support images into the query's domain (statistics-matched, mask-preserving) before matching.
main_risk: Restyling may corrupt fine-grained class evidence for texture-defined classes.

one_sentence_idea: Give few-shot/zero-shot segmenters a semantic-hierarchy fallback: when novel-class evidence is insufficient, output the most specific confident ancestor class ("vehicle" instead of a wrong "trailer").
main_risk: Hierarchy choice is contestable; partial-credit metric design needs care to avoid gaming.

one_sentence_idea: Transferable threshold calibration for open-vocabulary segmentation: learn how to set per-class confidence thresholds from base classes so novel classes get correct thresholds without any labels.
main_risk: Threshold predictability may vary by score head design, requiring per-architecture regressors.

one_sentence_idea: Make referring segmentation ambiguity-aware: when an expression matches multiple objects, output the candidate set plus a minimal clarifying question, instead of arbitrarily picking one.
main_risk: Constructed ambiguity may differ from natural ambiguity distributions.

one_sentence_idea: Use a learned part vocabulary as the transfer substrate for few-shot segmentation: novel objects are segmented by recognizing shared parts (legs, handles, wheels) plus a support-derived part composition.
main_risk: Unsupervised part discovery quality is the load-bearing dependency.

one_sentence_idea: Diagnose and fix support-query scale mismatch with a scale-searched matching pyramid whose scale posterior is output explicitly (the model reports at what scale it found the object).
main_risk: Extreme scale differences change effective appearance (texture visibility), beyond what search can fix.

one_sentence_idea: Settle when test-time fine-tuning on the support set helps versus hurts FSS, as a function of shot count, support-query domain gap, and parameter subset — producing a practitioner's decision table.
main_risk: Conclusions may shift with backbone scale, requiring at least two model sizes.

one_sentence_idea: Measure prototype interference in multi-way few-shot segmentation (N novel classes simultaneously) and correct it with joint prototype whitening/orthogonalization.
main_risk: Benchmarks with enough co-occurring classes per image are limited.

one_sentence_idea: Text-plus-shots division of labor: use language to solve recognition (which object) and the few shots only to define the boundary convention (how to delineate it).
main_risk: Some conventions may be spatially complex (not low-dimensional), breaking the premise.

one_sentence_idea: Replace research-convention episode sampling with deployment-realistic episode construction (supports chosen by non-experts, queries from operational distributions) and measure how method rankings change.
main_risk: Choice of noise models is contestable; needs grounding in a small real user study.

one_sentence_idea: Continual few-shot segmentation: enroll novel classes sequentially over months without storing past supports, using consolidated prototype memory with interference-aware placement.
main_risk: Long-horizon simulation may miss real temporal distribution drift.

one_sentence_idea: Map the support-annotation cost-quality frontier (points vs. boxes vs. polygons vs. precise masks per shot) to find the cost-optimal support labeling policy for a target accuracy.
main_risk: Cost constants vary across tools/annotators; report sensitivity analysis.

one_sentence_idea: Pretrain episodic segmentation ability entirely from unlabeled data by constructing pseudo-episodes from self-supervised clusters and mask proposals — no class labels ever.
main_risk: Cluster granularity may mismatch human class granularity, teaching wrong invariances.

one_sentence_idea: Support-sufficiency prediction: the model outputs, before segmenting, whether the provided supports are adequate for the query — enabling "ask for a better example" behavior.
main_risk: Sufficiency predictor may just learn query difficulty, not support-specific inadequacy (needs careful controls).

one_sentence_idea: Determine what learned soft prompts actually encode — class semantics or dataset-specific bias — via nearest-text projection and cross-dataset prompt-transplant experiments.
main_risk: Projection-based interpretation of continuous vectors is inherently contestable; needs multiple probes.

one_sentence_idea: Prevent prompt-tuning's characteristic collapse under distribution shift by regularizing learned prompts to stay on the natural-language embedding manifold.
main_risk: The text manifold may be poorly approximated by available anchors, weakening the constraint.

one_sentence_idea: Learn an automatic geometric-prompt policy (where to place points/boxes) for promptable segmenters, replacing grid prompting with a trained proposal agent optimized for downstream mask quality.
main_risk: Policy may overfit the specific promptable model version, requiring retraining per model release.

one_sentence_idea: Quantify prompt-position sensitivity of promptable segmenters (output variance across equivalent clicks inside the same object) and use that variance as a per-case failure predictor.
main_risk: Variance may conflate genuine ambiguity (multiple valid granularities) with instability; needs granularity-controlled analysis.

one_sentence_idea: Learn a mapping from acquisition/scene metadata (scanner tags, camera EXIF, weather) to prompt vectors, so a frozen dense model is domain-conditioned by free metadata instead of adapted on images.
main_risk: Metadata quality/completeness in the wild; mapper may shortcut on site identity rather than physical parameters.

one_sentence_idea: Prompt banks with per-input retrieval: maintain a library of specialized prompts (per condition/domain/subtask) and route each input to its nearest prompt by image content.
main_risk: Routing errors on boundary cases; bank growth management over time.

one_sentence_idea: Formalize negative prompting for dense prediction — "suppress X" prompts with a principled subtraction geometry in embedding space — to kill specific recurring false positives without retraining.
main_risk: Embedding arithmetic may not localize: suppressing "shadow" might damage semantically adjacent legitimate classes.

one_sentence_idea: Chain-of-prompts for nested structures: segment coarse-to-fine (organ → substructure → lesion) by conditioning each stage's prompt on the previous stage's output, with an explicit error-propagation study.
main_risk: Soft conditioning may blur stage responsibilities, making failures harder to attribute.

one_sentence_idea: Convention tokens: train one segmenter on multiple datasets with conflicting delineation conventions, exposing the convention as a switchable prompt, so one model serves all conventions on demand.
main_risk: Convention differences may be entangled with appearance differences between the datasets (needs controlled relabeling for a clean subset).

one_sentence_idea: Replace entropy-based test-time prompt tuning objectives with cross-augmentation agreement objectives, and characterize when each collapses.
main_risk: Augmentation choice becomes the new hidden hyperparameter (must be reported honestly).

one_sentence_idea: Prompt distillation: compress an ensemble of specialized prompts (or the prompting behavior of a large model) into a single compact prompt, quantifying what is lost.
main_risk: Results depend on prompt capacity (length), requiring a capacity sweep.

one_sentence_idea: Measure whether learned prompts transfer across backbone architectures, and if not, learn cheap prompt-translation adapters — establishing a science of prompt universality.
main_risk: Translation may only work between architecturally similar backbones.

one_sentence_idea: Instance-conditional prompts: a hypernetwork generates a per-input prompt from the image itself, tested against static prompts specifically under high intra-domain heterogeneity.
main_risk: Heterogeneity measurement itself requires care to avoid circularity.

one_sentence_idea: Uncertainty-eliciting prompts: learn prompts whose output channel is a calibrated per-pixel confidence for a frozen dense model, extracting reliability information the model has but does not express.
main_risk: The frozen model may genuinely lack the latent evidence, capping all conditioning approaches equally.

one_sentence_idea: Compare the adversarial and corruption robustness of prompt-tuned versus fully fine-tuned dense models at matched clean accuracy, testing whether the small prompt parameterization is a robustness feature.
main_risk: Matching clean accuracy exactly is fiddly; conclusions may depend on tuning budgets.

one_sentence_idea: Show that the training order of tasks/classes during multi-task prompt learning determines interference patterns, and derive an interference-minimizing prompt curriculum.
main_risk: Effects may be small in the frozen-backbone regime precisely because interference passes only through prompts.

one_sentence_idea: Textual inversion for domain jargon: learn pseudo-word embeddings for concepts VLMs don't know ("GGO", "slag inclusion", "delamination") from a few masked examples, enabling open-vocabulary segmentation of specialist vocabularies.
main_risk: Discriminative embedding spaces may be less compositional than generative ones.

one_sentence_idea: Pixel-space visual prompts (learnable border/frame perturbations) versus token-space prompts for adapting frozen dense models: map which adaptation regimes each can and cannot express.
main_risk: Optimization difficulty of pixel prompts may masquerade as expressivity limits (needs careful tuning).

one_sentence_idea: Systematize prompt ensembling for dense prediction: compare embedding-averaging, output-averaging, and learned aggregation, with a variance-decomposition explaining when each wins.
main_risk: Findings may be model-family-specific.

one_sentence_idea: Domain-incremental segmentation via prompt pools with key-based routing: each new domain adds a prompt, keys route inputs, and the frozen backbone guarantees zero interference on old domains.
main_risk: Key matching may fail on domains not seen by the (frozen) key encoder.

one_sentence_idea: Factorial study of prompt injection depth for dense tasks: establish where in the network prompts must enter to implement appearance conditioning versus semantic/task conditioning.
main_risk: Interactions with backbone architecture family (conv-hybrid vs. pure attention).

one_sentence_idea: Establish prompt-length scaling laws for dense tasks: performance and overfitting-onset as functions of token count and tuning-set size, yielding a practical sizing rule.
main_risk: The ratio may vary with task complexity, requiring a task-difficulty correction term.

one_sentence_idea: Gradient-free discrete prompt search for dense models (evolutionary/LLM-proposed hard prompts) as an interpretable, API-compatible alternative to soft prompts.
main_risk: Search cost (many evaluations); small labeled sets may overfit the search itself.

one_sentence_idea: Measure and improve compositional generalization of prompt-driven segmentation over attribute conjunctions ("cracked AND red region") via explicit prompt algebra.
main_risk: Attribute independence assumptions in the algebra fail for correlated attributes.

one_sentence_idea: One dense model, prompt-switchable across output tasks (semantic masks, instance boundaries, depth, normals) — measuring cross-task interference and synergy in the prompt regime.
main_risk: Frozen backbones may cap per-task ceilings below practical requirements.

one_sentence_idea: Region-conditioned prompting: combine spatial prompts ("in this region") with semantic prompts so reviewers can direct open-vocabulary segmentation to specific areas of interest.
main_risk: Training data for region-restricted supervision must be synthesized carefully to avoid shortcuts.

one_sentence_idea: Validation-free prompt overfitting detection: predict from prompt-space geometry (distance traveled from initialization, alignment with text manifold) whether a tuned prompt has overfit — no held-out data required.
main_risk: Signatures may be optimizer-dependent (learning rate confound).

one_sentence_idea: Quantify and close the cross-lingual gap in prompt-driven segmentation: do non-English class names (clinical Latin, German industrial terms) degrade dense predictions, and can multilingual prompt alignment fix it without retraining the VLM?
main_risk: Translation ambiguity of technical terms confounds measurement (needs curated term lists).

one_sentence_idea: Federated prompt personalization: sites share a frozen backbone and exchange only learned site-prompts, whose structure is then analyzed as an interpretable map of inter-site variation.
main_risk: Prompt averaging across genuinely incompatible domains may need mixture, not mean.

one_sentence_idea: Self-refinement loops for dense prediction: the model critiques its own segmentation (via a learned critique prompt) and emits a refined prompt for a second pass, with a learned stopping criterion.
main_risk: The critique may only see errors the model can already represent — blind spots persist through iterations.

one_sentence_idea: Measure the damage caused by out-of-distribution contamination in the unlabeled pool of semi-supervised segmentation, and build contamination-robust pseudo-labeling that filters by dual (feature + prediction-stability) criteria.
main_risk: Contamination taxonomy choices may not represent real dumps (mitigate with one genuinely raw hospital-style pool).

one_sentence_idea: Quantify pseudo-label error heritability across self-training generations (which errors persist, amplify, or die out) and design error-decorrelated co-training informed by the heritability map.
main_risk: Lineage tracking requires careful bookkeeping; conclusions may vary with threshold policies.

one_sentence_idea: Audit which consistency-regularization augmentations are label-semantics-preserving for medical images, and publish a validity-tested augmentation suite for anatomical data.
main_risk: Effects may be small at large labeled fractions (must test the low-label regime where SSL matters).

one_sentence_idea: Replace the fixed pseudo-label confidence threshold with per-class dynamic quantile thresholds matched to the labeled-set class distribution, rescuing rare classes from threshold starvation.
main_risk: Expected class frequencies estimated from small labeled sets are noisy; needs smoothing.

one_sentence_idea: Determine whether consistency regularization should operate in feature space or output space for dense prediction, with boundary quality as the discriminating metric.
main_risk: Interactions with augmentation strength could confound (control by factorial sub-design).

one_sentence_idea: Safe semi-supervised segmentation: pseudo-label inclusion governed by a statistical certificate ensuring the semi-supervised model is (with high confidence) no worse than the supervised-only baseline.
main_risk: Small validation sets make the sequential test conservative; the theory-practice gap in the certificate.

one_sentence_idea: Train segmentation from radiologists' eye-gaze recorded during routine reading, with a fixation-to-extent calibration model bridging the gap between where experts look and where lesions are.
main_risk: Gaze is contaminated by search behavior (looking at normal regions to rule things out).

one_sentence_idea: Mine weak 3D localization labels from the synchronization between dictation audio timestamps and image scroll/zoom positions during clinical reading.
main_risk: Reading styles vary (some dictate after scrolling away); requires per-reader noise modeling.

one_sentence_idea: Re-measure the scribble-supervision cost curve in the foundation-model era: how few scribbles suffice when combined with strong class-agnostic mask priors, and where does scribble information still matter?
main_risk: Results tied to specific prior models; needs 2+ priors for robustness.

one_sentence_idea: Centroid-only 3D lesion annotation: train segmentation from single center-point clicks per lesion with an expected-size prior and a count-preserving loss.
main_risk: Size priors mislead on atypical lesions; touching lesions break counting.

one_sentence_idea: Treat incompletely annotated datasets (only some lesions masked per scan) as positive-unlabeled learning, jointly estimating per-image annotation completeness and training an unbiased dense classifier.
main_risk: Real incompleteness is non-random (small/faint lesions skipped), harder than random decimation — needs a biased-decimation condition too.

one_sentence_idea: Sparse-slice 3D annotation with registration-guided label completion: annotate 3–5 optimally spaced slices per volume and complete labels via patient-specific deformable interpolation, training on completion-confidence-weighted targets.
main_risk: Registration quality varies with anatomy and pathology; the confidence model must be honest.

one_sentence_idea: Speckle-native self-supervised pretraining for ultrasound: pretext tasks built on speckle statistics (decorrelation prediction, statistics-map estimation) instead of natural-image SSL recipes that treat speckle as noise.
main_risk: Scanner post-processing (speckle reduction filters) may have already destroyed the statistics in available data.

one_sentence_idea: Confidence-gated temporal label propagation for medical video (ultrasound sweeps, endoscopy): quantify propagation error accumulation and admit propagated labels into training only where multi-cue gates agree.
main_risk: Gate signals may fail exactly during rapid probe motion where drift is worst.

one_sentence_idea: Value-based curation of the unlabeled pool: estimate each unlabeled sample's marginal value to semi-supervised training and show that curated subsets beat the full pool.
main_risk: Value scores may be method-dependent, requiring per-method calibration.

one_sentence_idea: Expose labeled-split variance in semi-supervised segmentation benchmarks: re-run standard protocols across many labeled-subset draws and test whether published method gaps exceed split noise.
main_risk: Compute cost; authors of affected methods will contest configurations.

one_sentence_idea: Test whether anatomically impossible mixing augmentations (CutMix/CopyPaste across patients) help or hurt medical semi-supervised segmentation, against the assumption that unrealistic mixes are harmless regularization.
main_risk: Layout corruption may only appear under distribution shift, requiring cross-site test sets.

one_sentence_idea: Correct unlabeled-pool class skew in semi-supervised segmentation by distribution-aligned crop sampling — sampling unlabeled crops to match the labeled class geography rather than uniformly.
main_risk: Early bad predictions could lock in wrong sampling (needs exploration floor).

one_sentence_idea: A stopping criterion for self-training rounds: predict the marginal gain of the next round from label-agreement statistics, ending the ritual of running a fixed number of rounds.
main_risk: The forecast may not transfer across method families without recalibration.

one_sentence_idea: Rigorously compare soft uncertainty-weighted consistency against hard confidence thresholding in dense SSL — a widely assumed superiority that has never been cleanly isolated.
main_risk: Calibration manipulation may covary with accuracy, confounding attribution.

one_sentence_idea: Co-training on genuinely independent views (frontal/lateral X-rays, multi-parametric MRI sequences) versus artificially augmented views, quantifying how much real view independence is worth.
main_risk: True views also differ in information content (not just independence), needing information-matched controls.

one_sentence_idea: Map how far single-atlas semi-supervision can go: one labeled volume + registration-propagated labels + modern self-training, benchmarked honestly against 10%-labeled baselines.
main_risk: Results heavily structure-dependent; must resist overgeneralizing from easy organs.

one_sentence_idea: Weakly supervised lesion localization by counterfactual comparison against a patient-matched normal appearance model, using only image-level "pathology present" labels.
main_risk: Normal-model quality varies across anatomy; deviation maps flag artifacts as pathology.

one_sentence_idea: Boundary-segment annotation: annotators trace only the boundary segments the model is uncertain about, with interiors and confident boundaries auto-completed — training on heterogeneous-density supervision.
main_risk: Real annotator time may not scale with tracing length as assumed (context acquisition overhead).

one_sentence_idea: Quantify patch-grid artifacts in ViT self-supervised features as a dense-prediction bottleneck and remove them via sub-patch offset-ensembled distillation.
main_risk: Distillation may smooth away genuine high-frequency features along with artifacts.

one_sentence_idea: Physics-based acquisition augmentation (simulated kernel, dose, sequence changes) as the consistency perturbation for medical semi-supervised learning, replacing photometric jitter.
main_risk: Simulation realism limits (see B-0011); some acquisition effects can't be simulated post hoc from images.

one_sentence_idea: Factorial dissection of noise types in noisy-student self-training for segmentation: which perturbation channel (input noise, feature dropout, label perturbation, depth/stochastic path) actually drives the dense-prediction gains.
main_risk: Interactions may require fractional-factorial extension; conclusions could be dataset-scale-dependent.

one_sentence_idea: Human verification (1-second accept/reject of pseudo-labels) as the supervision channel: quantify the value-per-second of verification versus annotation in dense SSL.
main_risk: Verification quality depends on display/UX; rejects may correlate with exactly the hard cases training needs.

one_sentence_idea: Longitudinal self-supervision from clinical archives: enforce prediction consistency on anatomy that a learned stability-detector deems unchanged between a patient's successive scans.
main_risk: Stability detector errors leak change into consistency targets, suppressing sensitivity to real change.

one_sentence_idea: Map the label-budget boundary where semi-supervised segmentation stops paying: a multi-task empirical law for when unlabeled data adds nothing over the labeled set alone.
main_risk: Conclusions tied to the chosen SSL method's strength; needs a second method for robustness.

one_sentence_idea: Audit mask-image misalignment in diffusion-generated segmentation training data and show that alignment-aware filtering beats generating more data.
main_risk: The alignment scorer's own biases could drive the filtering (use two independent scorers).

one_sentence_idea: Demonstrate and defeat the blending-artifact shortcut: models trained on lesions inpainted into healthy scans learn to detect inpainting boundaries, not lesions.
main_risk: Artifact detectability varies enormously across inpainting methods; needs several.

one_sentence_idea: Estimate the real-synthetic exchange rate — how many synthetic samples substitute for one real labeled sample — as a measurable function of generator, task, and domain.
main_risk: Exchange rates may depend on the real-data regime (helpful only below some real-data size), complicating the summary.

one_sentence_idea: Build a utility-predictive quality metric for synthetic segmentation data, benchmarked by correlation with actual downstream training gains — replacing FID, which predicts nothing about dense-task utility.
main_risk: Metric validity may not transfer across task families; needs held-out task validation.

one_sentence_idea: Label-first pathology synthesis: sample plausible label maps from anatomical+disease shape models, then render images conditioned on them — extending SynthSeg-style generation from anatomy to lesions with controllable rare-configuration coverage.
main_risk: Renderer quality on out-of-distribution label maps may degrade exactly where coverage is extended.

one_sentence_idea: Audit generative memorization leakage in synthetic medical datasets — near-copies of real patients surfacing in released synthetic sets — and its double harm: privacy breach and benchmark contamination.
main_risk: Embedding-based duplicate detection has contestable thresholds (mitigate with human verification of flagged pairs).

one_sentence_idea: Map the domain-randomization-versus-realism frontier for dense prediction: randomization wins when the target domain is unknown, realism when it is known — quantified as a function of target-domain knowledge.
main_risk: The dial's parameterization may not span the strategies fairly.

one_sentence_idea: Determine where synthetic data belongs in the training pipeline — pretraining, joint mixing, or fine-tuning stage — and whether the common "synthetic-then-real" curriculum is actually optimal.
main_risk: Conclusions may depend on relative volumes (needs a volume-ratio sweep).

one_sentence_idea: Counterfactual patient pairs — the same anatomy rendered with and without a lesion — as causal supervision that breaks co-occurrence shortcuts in lesion segmentation.
main_risk: Generation artifacts could introduce a new shortcut replacing the old one.

one_sentence_idea: Procedural (simulation-grown, generative-model-free) vascular and airway trees as topology-rich pretraining data for tubular-structure segmentation.
main_risk: Appearance gap may prevent transfer despite topological validity (test with appearance randomization).

one_sentence_idea: Confusion-conditioned hard-negative synthesis: generate near-miss negatives targeted at the model's current false-positive modes, as an adversarial curriculum for dense prediction.
main_risk: The verified-negative requirement (generated negatives must truly lack lesions) needs careful QC; loop may oscillate.

one_sentence_idea: Measure the thin-structure fidelity floor of latent diffusion (structures below which latent compression destroys them) and establish when pixel-space generation is required for training data.
main_risk: Conditioning may itself fail at thin widths, confounding generation vs. conditioning limits.

one_sentence_idea: Quantify when synthetic validation sets can be trusted for model selection: measure rank correlation between synthetic-val and real-val decisions across realistic model pools.
main_risk: Results depend on generator quality; needs a generator-quality sweep for the distance claim.

one_sentence_idea: Map the differential-privacy-versus-utility frontier for synthetic medical segmentation data: how much downstream Dice survives at meaningful privacy budgets.
main_risk: DP generative training is finicky; failures may reflect optimization rather than fundamental limits.

one_sentence_idea: Determine the minimum replay fidelity for generative replay in continual segmentation: how good must replayed synthetic data be to prevent forgetting of old tasks/domains?
main_risk: Axis degradations may not decompose cleanly (interactions).

one_sentence_idea: Factorial dissection of copy-paste augmentation harmonization: which components (lighting match, noise match, boundary blending, geometric plausibility) actually drive dense-prediction gains, and which merely hide detectable paste artifacts.
main_risk: Component effects may differ between natural and medical domains (run one of each).

one_sentence_idea: Class-wise utility prediction for text-to-image synthetic segmentation data: predict, per class, whether generation+cross-attention masks will help before training on them.
main_risk: Predictors may be model-version-specific, needing recalibration per generator release.

one_sentence_idea: Physics-based ultrasound simulation from CT/MRI-derived anatomy (with segmentation labels carried through) as a training source for ultrasound segmentation where real labeled data is scarce.
main_risk: Speckle and probe artifacts are notoriously hard to simulate faithfully (connects to B-0193's physics).

one_sentence_idea: Generate interpolated domains between training sources (synthetic domain bridging) and test whether filling the inter-domain gaps improves unseen-domain generalization more than adding same-domain volume.
main_risk: Interpolated domains may be off-manifold (unrealistic mixtures) and teach nothing relevant.

one_sentence_idea: Decompose synthetic data's advantage into label cleanliness versus image distribution: how much of the benefit is just that synthetic labels are perfect?
main_risk: Modeling "human-matched" label noise realistically requires multi-annotator data for calibration.

one_sentence_idea: Tail-targeted conditional generation for long-tail segmentation, with per-class gain accounting and identification of the class properties that make generation fail.
main_risk: Per-class gains at the tail are statistically noisy (see B-0277's power concern) — needs repeated runs.

one_sentence_idea: Pretrain a dense-prediction foundation model on 100% synthetic/procedural imagery (zero real data) and measure the real-data gap — a privacy-free, license-free FM baseline.
main_risk: Small-scale conclusions may not extrapolate to FM scale (same risk as B-0032; report as scaling trend).

one_sentence_idea: Simulate arbitrary MRI contrasts from quantitative tissue maps (qMRI) to train sequence-invariant segmentation, with physics-exact augmentation replacing style-transfer approximations.
main_risk: qMRI corpora are small and their own acquisition biases propagate into everything.

one_sentence_idea: Depth-consistent weather compositing for driving data: insert fog/rain with transmission computed from scene depth, and test whether physical consistency (vs. flat alpha overlays) matters for segmentation robustness transfer.
main_risk: Real-fog test sets are small; depth estimates in training data carry their own errors.

one_sentence_idea: Build generator blind-spot maps — a systematic catalog of visual phenomena a given generator cannot produce — and use them to predict where synthetic-trained models will fail and what real data to collect.
main_risk: Phenomenon battery completeness; blind spots may interact (compositional incapabilities).

one_sentence_idea: Measure synthetic-data scaling laws for dense prediction: the exponent and saturation point of performance versus synthetic volume, compared against real-data scaling on the same tasks.
main_risk: Compute cost of the sweep; exponents may vary with the real/synthetic ratio (add one ratio sweep).

one_sentence_idea: Condition generation on distance transforms instead of binary masks, hypothesizing sharper mask-image boundary agreement in synthetic segmentation data.
main_risk: Distance conditioning may trade boundary fidelity for interior realism.

one_sentence_idea: Decompose the sim-to-real gap into appearance versus content (layout/geometry) components via style-bridging experiments, to allocate generation-improvement effort where the gap actually lives.
main_risk: Style transfer imperfections blur the decomposition (bound them with the reverse control).

one_sentence_idea: Closed-loop self-improving synthesis: segmentation-model errors steer the next generation round, with an explicit study of convergence versus mode-collapse dynamics of the loop.
main_risk: Compute-intensive; conclusions may depend on error-to-conditioning translation quality.

one_sentence_idea: Validate generation-based stress testing: are controlled synthetic perturbation suites (same scene ± rain, occlusion sweeps) faithful proxies for real-perturbation robustness?
main_risk: "Matched" real conditions are hard to align in severity with synthetic sweeps (use ordinal matching).

one_sentence_idea: A sealed, cost-honest benchmark for active learning in segmentation — realistic batch sizes, cold starts, and time-based (not image-count) budgets — testing whether published AL gains survive.
main_risk: Cost-model choices are contestable (publish sensitivity analyses across cost models).

one_sentence_idea: Region-level active learning with a context-acquisition cost model: selecting small scattered regions is not cheap once the annotator must re-orient in each new image.
main_risk: Cost parameters vary across tools and annotator experience levels.

one_sentence_idea: Solve the active-learning cold-start problem for segmentation with self-supervised-feature coverage sampling — principled selection before any task model exists.
main_risk: SSL feature quality on the target domain gates everything (test with 2 feature sources).

one_sentence_idea: Measure automation-bias contamination in model-assisted annotation — annotators anchoring on pre-segmentations — and design blind-review protocols that keep the speed without inheriting the model's errors.
main_risk: Study effects (annotators behaving better when observed); needs naturalistic logging validation.

one_sentence_idea: Learn per-case annotation-time predictors and switch active learning from accuracy-per-image to accuracy-per-minute optimization.
main_risk: Time predictors may not transfer across annotators/tools without recalibration.

one_sentence_idea: Contestability prediction for annotation QA: train a model to predict which annotations a second expert would dispute, and route only those to re-review.
main_risk: Predictor may capture only generic ambiguity, missing annotator-specific lapses (complement with B-0268).

one_sentence_idea: Show that consensus label fusion (STAPLE-style) fails when raters share training lineage (correlated biases), and build lineage-aware fusion that models rater covariance.
main_risk: Recruiting lineage-controlled cohorts takes organization; effect may be structure-dependent.

one_sentence_idea: Learned slice-selection policies for 3D annotation: choose which slices a human should label (per volume, adaptively) to maximize full-volume label quality after completion.
main_risk: Policy training needs diverse dense-labeled volumes; gains may be organ-specific.

one_sentence_idea: Optimal coarse-to-fine annotation staging: label everything cheaply first, then spend refinement passes only where a model trained on coarse labels remains uncertain.
main_risk: Simulation-to-live gap in cost constants; stage-switching overhead.

one_sentence_idea: Establish when low-resolution annotation is safe: annotate at 4×-downsampled display, restore boundary precision with learned label super-resolution, and map the fidelity boundary by structure type.
main_risk: Annotator behavior at low resolution may change qualitatively (skipping small objects entirely).

one_sentence_idea: Unlock legacy datasets via learned ontology mapping: train converters between label protocols (different class definitions and granularities) so old annotations supervise new tasks with quantified fidelity.
main_risk: Some protocol differences depend on information absent from images (clinical context), capping conversion.

one_sentence_idea: Validate learning-curve extrapolation as a budgeting instrument for dense tasks: from a small pilot annotation, predict the accuracy-versus-N curve before committing the campaign budget.
main_risk: Extrapolation may fail exactly for the novel tasks where budgeting matters most (report domain-transfer validity).

one_sentence_idea: Quantify the deployment bias created by "interesting-case" annotation (skipping easy/normal cases) and correct it with importance weighting plus a mandatory random floor.
main_risk: Real selection processes are less documented than simulated ones (the selection model must be estimated).

one_sentence_idea: Sequential stopping rules for annotation campaigns: monitor marginal model improvement per label batch and stop when the campaign's remaining value drops below its cost, with statistical guarantees.
main_risk: Non-stationary campaigns (annotator mix changes over time) violate monitor assumptions.

one_sentence_idea: Measure the gap between simulated and real users in interactive-segmentation evaluation, then build empirically calibrated user models — because current click simulators may be crowning the wrong methods.
main_risk: User-study variance requires careful within-subject design; tool-UX confounds method comparison.

one_sentence_idea: Optimize the propagate-verify economics of video annotation: find the keyframe density and verification policy that minimize total human time for target label quality.
main_risk: Results depend on tracker generation; must report against 2 trackers.

one_sentence_idea: Speech-first annotation: the annotator describes the target verbally ("the darker nodule under the pleura, not the vessel"), a grounding model proposes the mask, and the human verifies — replacing tracing with talking.
main_risk: Grounding-model errors on specialist vocabulary (mitigable via B-0167's pseudo-words).

one_sentence_idea: Difficulty-based annotator routing: predict per-case difficulty and route cases between crowd workers and experts to hit target quality at minimum cost.
main_risk: Crowd availability/ethics for medical images; difficulty predictor drift across case-mix changes.

one_sentence_idea: Estimate the per-class marginal value of the next annotation and allocate labeling budgets across classes by marginal return, not by prevalence or uniformity.
main_risk: Per-class slope estimation is noisy early, when allocation matters most (hence the hierarchical smoothing).

one_sentence_idea: Statistical process control for annotation quality: continuously double-annotate a small hidden audit stream to track dataset error rate live, with control-chart triggers for intervention.
main_risk: Hidden auditing raises consent/ethics questions in some annotator arrangements.

one_sentence_idea: Validate micro-verification as a supervision channel: 3-second binary questions ("is the boundary correct in this circle?") aggregated across many viewers into training-grade boundary supervision.
main_risk: Question placement is a chicken-and-egg with model uncertainty quality.

one_sentence_idea: Train on imperfect labels by modeling each annotator's error process (systematic over/under-segmentation, boundary style) and inverting it — annotator-ID-conditioned training instead of label cleaning.
main_risk: Requires several annotations per annotator; identifiability issues if annotators saw disjoint case types.

one_sentence_idea: Measure how annotation-tool interaction latency and rendering quality causally affect label accuracy — the tool as an uncontrolled variable in every dataset.
main_risk: Lab conditions may understate long-session effects (fatigue-latency interactions).

one_sentence_idea: Find the pre-annotation quality threshold: below what model quality does showing pre-segmentations slow annotators down or corrupt labels, versus starting blank?
main_risk: Threshold likely varies across annotator skill (stratify by experience).
