one_sentence_idea: Test whether many cheap coarse masks aggregate to expert precision: crowd consensus of low-effort annotations versus single expert masks, evaluated boundary-wise.
main_risk: Crowd platform quality variance; instructions confound (fix via single protocol).

one_sentence_idea: Correspondence-based label transfer to new datasets: match unlabeled images to labeled-archive neighbors via dense correspondence, warp their labels across, and have humans verify — annotation as retrieval-plus-verification.
main_risk: Archive-target license and distribution mismatches; correspondence fails exactly on novel content (by design, triaged out).

one_sentence_idea: Systematically detect and correct label errors in legacy segmentation benchmarks, then re-rank state-of-the-art methods on the cleaned versions.
main_risk: Corrections themselves embed judgment calls (publish both versions with provenance).

one_sentence_idea: Estimate per-annotator reliability without any gold standard, purely from the structure of the agreement graph across overlapping assignments, and weight label fusion accordingly.
main_risk: Requires overlap structure in assignments (design constraint on campaigns).

one_sentence_idea: Treat annotation-guideline wording as an experimental variable: controlled guideline A/B tests measuring how phrasing and example choice shift the resulting labels.
main_risk: Effects may be structure-specific; needs replication on 2–3 structures.

one_sentence_idea: Solve the annotation-portfolio problem: given a fixed budget, optimize the mix of expert masks, crowd coarse labels, verification passes, and synthetic data against a validated end-to-end model-quality objective.
main_risk: Interaction terms may be strong and task-specific, limiting transferability of the optimizer.

one_sentence_idea: Disentangle the three conflated imbalance axes in long-tail segmentation — image frequency, instance frequency, and pixel area — and show each requires a different remedy.
main_risk: Perfect axis isolation is impossible (correlations remain); report achieved decorrelation.

one_sentence_idea: Demonstrate that image-level resampling — the standard long-tail remedy — barely changes pixel-level class exposure in segmentation, and replace it with crop-level rebalancing.
main_risk: Aggressive crop rebalancing distorts context statistics (interacts with B-0276; control context in crops).

one_sentence_idea: Measure the collateral damage of loss reweighting on head-class boundary quality and calibration, and fix it with interior-only reweighting that spares boundary pixels.
main_risk: Interior/boundary partition adds a hyperparameter (band width); results may vary with class geometry.

one_sentence_idea: Run the statistical power analysis of long-tail benchmarks: with a handful of test instances per tail class, published per-class improvements may be statistically meaningless — quantify and fix the reporting.
main_risk: Authors may dispute bootstrap assumptions for structured outputs (use block bootstrap over images).

one_sentence_idea: Test whether the decoupling result from long-tail classification (representations are fine, only the classifier needs rebalancing) transfers to dense prediction, where the "classifier" is a spatial decoder.
main_risk: Results may depend on decoder capacity (sweep two decoder sizes).

one_sentence_idea: Quantify contextual imprisonment of tail classes — rare classes recognized only in their most typical context — and break it with context-decorrelation training.
main_risk: Compositing artifacts confound (use B-0226's artifact controls).

one_sentence_idea: Transfer intra-class variation from head to tail: learn variation modes (pose, lighting, style deformations) on head classes and apply them as feature-space augmentation to tail classes.
main_risk: Class-specific variation (deformations unique to the tail class) is not covered — bounds the achievable gain.

one_sentence_idea: Label borrowing through class hierarchies: supervise tail classes jointly with abundant superclass labels (every "rare terrier" is also a "dog"), quantifying how much hierarchy-mediated supervision closes the tail gap.
main_risk: Incoherent superclasses ("miscellaneous") could actively hurt (the stratification tests this).

one_sentence_idea: Map when mixture-of-experts beats unified models for long-tail segmentation: dedicated tail experts with learned routing versus one shared model, as a function of tail-head feature conflict.
main_risk: Gradient-conflict metrics are noisy and training-stage-dependent.

one_sentence_idea: Hybrid parametric/non-parametric prediction: head classes served by the trained decoder, tail classes by k-NN retrieval over a labeled feature memory — because parametric compression is exactly what scarce classes can't afford.
main_risk: Retrieval latency at inference; memory feature drift if the backbone is later updated.

one_sentence_idea: Context-matched copy-paste for tail classes: paste rare objects into contexts sampled from a learned plausibility model, testing the claim that context diversity (not paste count) drives tail gains.
main_risk: Plausibility model errors create harmful implausible composites (monitor with a plausibility-quality sweep).

one_sentence_idea: Characterize calibration as a function of class frequency in segmentation and deploy frequency-conditional recalibration — because a single temperature cannot fix a frequency-structured miscalibration.
main_risk: Tail calibration estimates are noisy (same power problem as B-0274; use aggregated frequency bins).

one_sentence_idea: Measure the tension between long-tail recognition and open-set detection: methods that boost rare-known-class confidence plausibly destroy the ability to flag never-seen classes.
main_risk: Unknown-class choice affects the frontier's shape (use multiple unknown splits).

one_sentence_idea: Federated long-tail segmentation: when every site has a different tail, federated averaging erases all of them — fix with shared trunk plus site-personalized tail heads and cross-site tail-knowledge exchange.
main_risk: Feature-exemplar sharing needs its own privacy audit (connects to B-0115/B-0040).

one_sentence_idea: Rare anatomical variants as medical long-tail: build a variant-enriched evaluation (situs inversus, accessory organs, post-surgical anatomy) and a variant-detection safety layer that flags when standard models should not be trusted.
main_risk: Variant case collection is laborious; some variants are individually so rare that even the safety evaluation is underpowered.

one_sentence_idea: Extend post-hoc logit adjustment to structured dense outputs: frequency-corrected decision rules for segmentation applied at inference, no retraining.
main_risk: Image-level prior estimation errors could hurt individual images (bound with conservative priors).

one_sentence_idea: Determine the effective sample-size law for dense tasks: which quantity — instance count, pixel area, or context/appearance diversity — actually predicts tail-class learnability.
main_risk: Diversity measures are feature-space-dependent (replicate with two feature sources).

one_sentence_idea: Isolate tail boundary quality: rare classes suffer disproportionately worse boundaries even when recognized, and class-agnostic boundary transfer from head classes can fix it.
main_risk: Confounding between class frequency and intrinsic boundary difficulty (control with matched-geometry class pairs).

one_sentence_idea: Zero-frequency classes via compositional description — segmenting classes with zero training instances from attribute compositions — with hallucination rate as a first-class reported metric.
main_risk: Verifying true absence in evaluation images requires careful curation.

one_sentence_idea: Targeted tail collection via retrieval: mine unlabeled archives/web for probable tail-class instances with open-vocabulary detectors, route to verification, and compare cost-per-useful-tail-sample against annotating random data.
main_risk: Retrieval works precisely for classes the detector already knows — the hardest tails stay hard (report the retrievability boundary).

one_sentence_idea: Controlled study of sampling-temperature schedules for long-tail segmentation: does annealing from natural to balanced distribution beat any static mixture, and why?
main_risk: Interactions with learning-rate schedules confound (factorial sub-design needed).

one_sentence_idea: Compositional long-tail: build evaluation and methods for rare class-attribute combinations (rusty car, flooded road) that class-level long-tail analysis cannot see.
main_risk: Attribute annotation sparsity limits cell coverage (supplement with targeted annotation).

one_sentence_idea: Measure per-class effective capacity usage in segmentation networks and test whether explicitly reallocating capacity (wider tail-specific pathways) beats loss-based rebalancing.
main_risk: Capacity metrics are indirect; architectural interventions change more than capacity (control carefully).

one_sentence_idea: Quantify the label-noise/long-tail interaction: a fixed label-error rate destroys tail classes disproportionately, and noise-robust methods must be evaluated per frequency stratum.
main_risk: Synthetic noise may differ from real annotation errors (add one real-noise condition via B-0267's error mining).

one_sentence_idea: Tail discovery in unlabeled pools: use open-set/novelty scoring to surface probable rare-class instances from unlabeled data for human confirmation, growing the tail's labeled set at minimum verification cost.
main_risk: Discovery favors prototypical tail instances (same diversity penalty as B-0290 — measure it).

one_sentence_idea: Replace frequency-blind mIoU with deployment-utility-weighted evaluation for long-tail segmentation, and show that method rankings depend strongly on the utility model.
main_risk: Utility models are contestable (publish them as replaceable modules, report sensitivity).

one_sentence_idea: Measure the order of forgetting during fine-tuning — tail classes are erased first — and build tail-protective fine-tuning that shields frequency-critical parameters.
main_risk: Frequency confounds with learnability (control by matching initial per-class accuracy).

one_sentence_idea: Intra-class tails: discover rare sub-modes within head classes (unusual poses, rare sub-types) via feature clustering, and rebalance at sub-mode level — long-tail treatment below the label granularity.
main_risk: Clusters may capture nuisance factors (background) rather than meaningful sub-modes.

one_sentence_idea: Decompose per-tail-class failure into detectability versus delineability — some rare classes are found-but-mistraced, others missed-entirely — and route each to its matching remedy.
main_risk: Small per-class test counts limit typing confidence (aggregate by predicted type, per B-0274).

one_sentence_idea: Fit the collection scaling law for tail classes: marginal accuracy per additional labeled sample as a function of current class frequency, enabling principled collection budgets per class.
main_risk: Difficulty offsets may dominate the shared structure, leaving predictions too loose to guide budgets.

one_sentence_idea: Decompose exactly what transfers from natural-image pretraining to medical segmentation — low-level edge machinery versus semantic organization — via layer-wise transplant-and-freeze experiments.
main_risk: Layer-wise attribution is entangled with optimization effects (control with multiple learning-rate regimes).

one_sentence_idea: Establish the science of 2D→3D weight inflation: which inflation strategy wins, when inflation beats native 3D pretraining, and what property of the 2D source predicts inflated performance.
main_risk: Conclusions may shift with architecture family (test conv and transformer variants).

one_sentence_idea: Transfer video models to volumes: treat the through-plane axis as time and test whether temporal inductive biases (motion smoothness, tracking) map onto anatomical continuity.
main_risk: Video models' frame-rate assumptions may mismatch slice spacing (test spacing-conditioned variants per B-0001).

one_sentence_idea: Cross-spectral transfer surgery: identify which pretrained-feature channels break under RGB→thermal/NIR transfer and repair them with channel-statistics reinitialization rather than full fine-tuning.
main_risk: Channel entanglement in modern backbones may blur the broken/intact distinction.

one_sentence_idea: Settle stain transfer versus stain-invariant training in histopathology with a controlled same-tissue comparison, and decompose the residual gap after each.
main_risk: Same-tissue multi-stain data is limited (may need one collaborating lab).

one_sentence_idea: Attribute the histopathology scanner gap to its physical components — optics (PSF, focus), color pipeline, and compression — via component-wise simulation, enabling targeted physics-informed calibration transfer.
main_risk: Component interactions (focus × compression) may break additivity.

one_sentence_idea: Human→animal medical transfer along anatomical homology: use evolutionary homology maps as the transfer prior and test whether transfer quality tracks homology distance.
main_risk: Species differences in imaging protocols confound anatomy effects (control by protocol matching).

one_sentence_idea: Build the dense-task transfer matrix: measure pairwise transfer value among segmentation, depth, normals, and boundary tasks across domains, testing whether geometric-task pretraining specifically improves segmentation boundaries.
main_risk: Matrix entries may depend on pretraining scale (report at two scales).

one_sentence_idea: Measure inter-domain gradient conflict in multi-domain segmentation training and fix it with conflict-aware batch composition, rather than architectural separation.
main_risk: Conflict metrics fluctuate through training; scheduling gains may not survive learning-rate interactions.

one_sentence_idea: Adapter arithmetic for unseen domains: compose adapters trained on multiple seen domains (weighted combinations) to handle novel domains, testing whether domain adaptation is compositional in adapter space.
main_risk: Factor interactions in image formation (fog at night ≠ fog + night) may dominate.

one_sentence_idea: Determine when weight-space merging of domain-expert segmentation models works: the feature-alignment precondition for model soups across domains.
main_risk: Dense decoders may be less linearly connected than classifiers, making the useful regime narrow.

one_sentence_idea: Language as the alignment bridge for cross-domain dense transfer when no paired or even unpaired image correspondence exists — align both domains' features to shared text anchors.
main_risk: Text anchors are coarse (region-level), possibly capping boundary quality (combine with class-agnostic boundary modules per B-0288).

one_sentence_idea: Benchmark domain-distance metrics as transfer predictors: which cheap measurement between source and target best predicts realized fine-tuning gain across many domain pairs — building a validated "transferability oracle" for dense tasks.
main_risk: The pair sample may under-represent extreme gaps; predictor may overfit dataset families.

one_sentence_idea: Detect negative transfer before paying for it: build predictors for when pretrained initialization hurts dense-task training relative to from-scratch, and characterize the negative-transfer regime.
main_risk: Regime boundaries may shift with optimization recipes (report across two recipes).

one_sentence_idea: Validated checkpoint selection from model zoos for dense tasks: race cheap proxies (frozen-feature probing, gradient measures) against exhaustive fine-tuning as selection oracles.
main_risk: Reference fine-tuning quality itself varies with budget (fix budgets carefully).

one_sentence_idea: Test whether generative (diffusion) model features are more domain-robust dense representations than discriminative features — and localize where each wins across the shift spectrum.
main_risk: Matching model scale/data across paradigms is hard; conclusions may be scale-dependent.

one_sentence_idea: Characteristic-scale mismatch in cross-domain transfer (satellite→drone→ground): measure the transfer cost of object-scale distribution shifts and fix it with scale-canonicalizing input pyramids rather than fine-tuning.
main_risk: Scale estimation errors on heterogeneous scenes; residual appearance gaps still need handling.

one_sentence_idea: Cross-domain distillation without paired data: transfer a teacher's dense knowledge to a student in a different domain via relational (feature-geometry) targets instead of per-pixel matching.
main_risk: Relation structures may be domain-contingent (class co-occurrence differs), teaching wrong priors.

one_sentence_idea: Test the anomaly-segmentation universality hypothesis: joint training on industrial defects and medical lesions improves both, because both tasks share a "deviation from learned normality" core.
main_risk: Domain interference (per B-0309) could mask genuine shared structure (control batch composition).

one_sentence_idea: Layout canonicalization for viewpoint transfer: correct the layout-statistics rotation between overhead and ground views (sky-above priors vs. map-like priors) before transfer, isolating layout from appearance in viewpoint gaps.
main_risk: Layout and appearance layers may not separate cleanly in modern architectures.

one_sentence_idea: Decompose the dermoscopy↔clinical-photo gap within the same disease: which acquisition component (optics/magnification, illumination geometry, framing/distance, calibration) dominates transfer failure for skin lesion segmentation.
main_risk: Paired data volume is modest; factor simulations approximate reality imperfectly.

one_sentence_idea: Exploit patient-paired multi-modal datasets (fundus + OCT of the same eyes) for supervised cross-modal representation alignment, enabling label transfer between modalities without any target-modality annotation.
main_risk: Geometric correspondence between modalities is partial (2D fundus vs. 3D OCT), bounding transferable structures.

one_sentence_idea: Factorial sim-to-real for surgical scenes: determine which simulator deficiencies (specular wetness, tissue deformation, smoke/irrigation, texture realism) actually block simulator-trained surgical segmentation.
main_risk: Factor interactions; real-data evaluation sets are small (use multiple).

one_sentence_idea: Stepwise transfer through constructed intermediate domains: test when a bridging-domain curriculum (photo→edge-map→sketch) beats direct fine-tuning across large gaps, and how to choose the path.
main_risk: Bridge quality confounds step-count effects (control bridge construction method).

one_sentence_idea: Map where domain gaps live in frequency space across many domain pairs, and use each pair's band-signature as a transfer diagnostic that selects the appropriate adaptation method.
main_risk: Band swapping introduces artifacts that contaminate the measurement (use soft band interpolation).

one_sentence_idea: Derive the freeze-depth law for cross-domain fine-tuning: how many backbone layers to unfreeze as a function of measured domain distance and target data size, validated as a practitioner's rule.
main_risk: Interaction with adapter-style alternatives (report against PEFT baselines per B-0038).

one_sentence_idea: Audit "universal" segmentation models on verifiably held-out domains and publish domain-coverage cartography: where universality claims actually hold.
main_risk: Training-distribution details of closed models are opaque (estimate proximity via behavioral probes).

one_sentence_idea: Fit the annotation-versus-distance law for porting: the minimum target annotation needed to close a cross-domain gap as a function of measured domain distance — pricing every port in labels.
main_risk: Target-accuracy choice affects the law's shape (report at multiple thresholds).

one_sentence_idea: Quantify the cost of shared normalization statistics in multi-domain training and establish when domain-conditional normalization is necessary versus wasteful.
main_risk: Threshold may depend on normalization type (BN/LN/GN — test all three).

one_sentence_idea: Test whether robustness transfers independently of accuracy: does corruption/adversarial tolerance acquired in a source domain survive fine-tuning into a target domain, or must robustness be re-trained per domain?
main_risk: Robustness metrics across domains need careful severity matching.

one_sentence_idea: Mine negations from radiology reports ("no pneumothorax", "unremarkable liver") into certified-negative spatial supervision — the report's most reliable content, currently discarded.
main_risk: Atlas grounding errors turn good negations into wrong negative labels (bound with conservative region margins).

one_sentence_idea: Use size measurements quoted in reports ("2.3 cm nodule") as metric supervision: the predicted lesion's differentiable diameter must match the reported number.
main_risk: Report measurements have their own error/rounding conventions; matching measured lesion to predicted instance is nontrivial in multi-lesion cases.

one_sentence_idea: Ground anatomical location phrases ("left lower lobe", "segment VII") into atlas-defined spatial priors as coarse but abundant localization supervision for dense models.
main_risk: Atlas registration errors on abnormal anatomy (exactly where findings are) weaken constraints.

one_sentence_idea: Convert report hedging language ("possibly", "cannot exclude", "likely") into calibrated uncertainty labels, training segmentation models whose confidence mirrors the radiologist's expressed certainty.
main_risk: Hedging conventions vary across radiologists/institutions (model reader effects per B-0262's philosophy).

one_sentence_idea: Mine temporal comparison statements ("increased from prior", "stable") into ordinal longitudinal supervision linking study pairs — training change-aware segmentation without any change masks.
main_risk: Comparatives sometimes reference different lesions than the model tracks (instance-matching ambiguity).

one_sentence_idea: Measure and de-bias template leakage in report-supervised models: models shortcut on institutional boilerplate ("PORTABLE study; lines and tubes...") instead of learning image-grounded semantics.
main_risk: Finding extraction may discard genuinely useful context along with boilerplate.

one_sentence_idea: Word-region alignment via optimal transport for report-supervised dense training, with phrase grounding as the audited intermediate rather than an emergent hope.
main_risk: Grounded evaluation subsets are small; OT costs need anatomical priors to avoid degenerate couplings.

one_sentence_idea: Extract lesion counts from reports ("three hepatic metastases") as instance-count constraints for multi-lesion segmentation training.
main_risk: Reports count what radiologists deem reportable (size thresholds), a systematic bias needing a threshold model.

one_sentence_idea: Diagnose exactly why CLIP-style patch tokens are poor at dense tasks — training-objective-induced global pooling artifacts versus data-induced deficits — and repair them by dense-alignment self-distillation with the diagnosis as the guide.
main_risk: Small-scale VLM findings may not extrapolate to production-scale models (validate signatures on public large models).

one_sentence_idea: Exploit depth-boundary coincidence as free supervision: depth discontinuities from RGB-D or stereo mark object boundaries, refining segmentation boundaries without any mask labels.
main_risk: Depth edges mark occlusions, not semantic boundaries — the divergence cases need the gating to work.

one_sentence_idea: Alignment-robust cross-modal distillation: characterize how much spatial misregistration between teacher modality (thermal/depth) and student modality (RGB) distillation can tolerate, and design losses that degrade gracefully.
main_risk: Synthetic misregistration may miss real error structure (validate on one genuinely uncalibrated rig).

one_sentence_idea: Establish the modality-dropout curriculum: how the schedule of missing-modality simulation during training (constant rate, annealed, blockwise) shapes robustness to missing inputs at deployment.
main_risk: Optimal schedules may vary with modality count/redundancy (test two modality sets).

one_sentence_idea: Surgeon commentary as supervision: align intraoperative speech ("now dividing the cystic duct") with surgical video to weakly supervise instrument and anatomy segmentation.
main_risk: Narration is sparse and anticipatory/retrospective (speech precedes or follows the visible act) — temporal offset modeling required.

one_sentence_idea: Mine historical radiotherapy dose maps and plans as free dense supervision: clinically approved dose distributions encode organ-at-risk and target geometry with life-critical precision.
main_risk: Dose shaping reflects planning trade-offs, not pure anatomy (margins, sparing priorities) — requires a plan-convention model.

one_sentence_idea: Use PET uptake (SUV maps) as soft supervision for CT tumor segmentation in paired PET/CT — metabolic evidence teaching anatomical delineation.
main_risk: Uptake is not coextensive with tumor (necrotic cores, inflammation) — the calibration model carries the burden.

one_sentence_idea: Quantify how LLM parsing errors propagate into dense supervision: the noise budget of the increasingly universal reports-to-structured-tuples-to-labels pipeline.
main_risk: Real LLM errors correlate with report difficulty (validate injection realism against measured LLM error distributions).

one_sentence_idea: Build an instruction-following benchmark for dense medical prediction: do "segment anything you describe" models actually execute clinical instructions (modifiers, exclusions, conditionals), or only class names?
main_risk: Programmatic instruction generation may not match clinical phrasing (validate with clinician-written instructions).

one_sentence_idea: Condition lesion segmentation on patient covariates (labs, demographics, history) as prior-shifting context — and rigorously separate legitimate prior use from harmful shortcut dependence.
main_risk: Covariate-outcome correlations in retrospective data may be irreducibly confounded (choose covariates with known mechanistic relevance).

one_sentence_idea: A principled fusion framework for multiple weak supervision modalities (gaze, report text, clicks, dose maps) with unknown, correlated error structures — measuring complementarity instead of assuming it.
main_risk: Spatial error correlation estimation may need more channel overlap than archives provide.

one_sentence_idea: Audit suggestion-induced hallucination in text-conditioned medical segmentation: does asking for a finding make the model draw one that isn't there?
main_risk: Verifying absence requires careful adjudication (reuse negation-verified cases).

one_sentence_idea: Free-text acquisition context ("portable AP view, patient rotated, limited study") as conditioning input for dense models — the unstructured sibling of DICOM metadata conditioning.
main_risk: Comments correlate with case difficulty (condition may just learn "be uncertain" — distinguish via calibration analysis).

one_sentence_idea: Sentence-to-region contrastive pretraining: align individual report sentences with image regions (instead of whole reports with whole images) and measure the dense-task value of alignment granularity.
main_risk: Sentence-region pairing without ground truth is itself noisy (the OT machinery of B-0337 is the pairing engine).

one_sentence_idea: Doppler audio as vessel supervision: the audio stream of Doppler ultrasound encodes flow presence and velocity — use it as free supervision for vessel segmentation in B-mode images.
main_risk: Gate positions sample vessels sparsely and non-randomly (operators interrogate where they already see vessels).

one_sentence_idea: Quantify the supervision value of structured reporting: how much more dense-training signal per report does structured reporting (organ/finding/segment fields) yield versus free text — evidence to inform reporting policy.
main_risk: Corpora with parallel structured/free-text reporting are limited (some registries qualify).

one_sentence_idea: Multimodal consistency as a deployment QC loop: disagreement between report-derived expectations and image-derived segmentation flags errors in either the model or the report — one signal auditing both.
main_risk: Correlated failures (model trained on similar reports misses what reports miss — B-0336's shortcut) blind the loop exactly where both err.

one_sentence_idea: Let a physically grounded modality define the boundary convention for an ambiguous one: elastography stiffness maps as the training-time arbiter of tumor boundaries in B-mode ultrasound and MRI.
main_risk: Elastography has its own artifacts and limited penetration; registration between modalities on deformable tissue is hard.

one_sentence_idea: Mine RECIST caliper annotations — the diameter lines radiologists draw on millions of oncology studies — as sparse geometric supervision for lesion segmentation at archive scale.
main_risk: Real calipers have selection bias (target lesions only per RECIST rules) — the PU machinery of B-0191 handles the unmeasured lesions.

one_sentence_idea: Settle whether report generation as an auxiliary task improves dense-prediction representations — the transfer direction the medical VLM field assumes but has not isolated.
main_risk: Grounding enforcement mechanisms themselves add supervision (control by grounding-without-generation arm).

one_sentence_idea: Pathology-outcome-anchored supervision: use downstream ground truth (biopsy results, resected-specimen measurements) as delayed, sparse, but definitionally correct labels correcting segmentation trained on imaging conventions.
main_risk: Resection cohorts are selected (operable cases), and specimen processing changes geometry (shrinkage models required).

one_sentence_idea: A grounding-capability taxonomy for medical vision-language segmenters: systematically measure what current models actually ground — anatomy terms, finding terms, spatial modifiers, quantities — as the diagnostic foundation for the report-supervision program.
main_risk: Category boundaries are fuzzy (publish the taxonomy with the benchmark for community iteration).

one_sentence_idea: Test whether ambiguity handling is one transferable skill: does a model trained to express uncertainty on multi-rater medical boundaries transfer that competence to smoke boundaries and camouflage, or is ambiguity handling domain-bound?
main_risk: Requires multi-rater data in several domains (B-0070's collection feeds this).

one_sentence_idea: Measure the metric-decision correlation: which segmentation metric improvements actually change downstream decisions (treatment choice, alarm raised, robot action), and how much published "progress" is decision-invisible.
main_risk: Decision rules vary across institutions (use several; report sensitivity).

one_sentence_idea: Efficiency-normalized progress audit: re-rank recent dense-prediction state of the art under matched inference compute/energy budgets and measure how much claimed progress survives.
main_risk: Faithful re-implementation and measurement standardization burden (publish the harness).

one_sentence_idea: Reproducibility audit of dense-prediction SOTA: quantify how much of published method-over-baseline gaps survives independent reimplementation, seed variance, and tuned baselines.
main_risk: Reimplementation fidelity disputes (mitigate with author-reviewed configurations and released code).

one_sentence_idea: A standardized uncertainty-evaluation protocol for dense prediction — calibration, spatial structure, and downstream utility measured jointly — adopted as a reporting standard across all task families in this catalog.
main_risk: Utility-axis design requires workflow assumptions (publish as configurable modules).

one_sentence_idea: Simulate the multi-generation dataset ecosystem: models assist annotation, the resulting datasets train the next models, which assist the next annotation — measuring whether dense-prediction data ecosystems drift toward model-error fixation ("annotation collapse").
main_risk: Simulation fidelity to real annotator behavior (anchor parameters must come from real studies, hence the dependency on B-0244).
